title: Maintain one living optimization run report
description:
As an account operator, I want one durable report to follow a periodic optimization run, so that the status and evidence remain available at one stable location.

Feature: Living optimization run report

Scenario: Start and update one report
  Given a periodic optimization run with a frozen scope and time window
  When the run publishes successive milestones
  Then one running task and one report are reused
  And each milestone appears in the existing report
  And immutable evidence revisions remain available

Scenario: Fail on report divergence
  Given a periodic optimization run has advanced
  When its report milestone cannot be durably published
  Then the run fails
  And it does not continue with stakeholder state behind procedure state

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented outside-in coverage and the initial service slice: one Task/Report per explicit run key; three fixed ReportBlocks; attachment-backed compact envelopes from initialization; immutable JSON/XLSX revisions; recovery reuse; and fatal milestone publication failure marks the Task failed. Focused tests are green.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Hardening pass: separate deterministic run identity from attempt identity; resume only active attempts; keep terminal failed or blocked attempts immutable and link retries; add fixed TaskStages and complete terminal-state semantics. Artifact publication will use only application-authorized GraphQL tickets: restricted evidence as Task attachments and public revisions as ReportBlock attachments. No direct S3 fallback.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Hardening implementation complete locally: deterministic run key plus distinct attempt IDs; active-attempt resume; immutable failed/blocked attempts with linked successor Tasks/Reports; eight fixed TaskStages; real initial workbook; append-only full revision metadata; standardized terminal states; fatal publication. Restricted evidence now uses existing Task attachment tickets and public revision files use existing ReportBlock tickets. No direct-S3 fallback.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Zero-infrastructure correction: all living-report artifacts (restricted evidence, workbook revisions, and manifests) will use the existing Task attachment ticket route and Task object keys. ReportBlocks will retain only compact attachment-pointer envelopes. The temporary ReportBlock ticket route and all backend changes will be removed so this slice has zero backend/schema/resource diff.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Zero-infrastructure correction completed locally. Initialization files and every evidence/workbook/manifest revision now flow through one existing TASK_ATTACHMENT route using the attempt Task ID. Task.attachedFiles retains the immutable keys; each ReportBlock stores only its compact pointer envelope. The temporary ReportBlock ticket/backend changes were removed and the backend/resolver/test files are byte-identical to base.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Validation update: the zero-resource working diff has no Amplify/schema/resource/function/storage changes and no ActionRequest/ActionEvent references. A model-backed sandbox run completed through finalization with six immutable TASK_ATTACHMENT revisions; the final eight-sheet workbook reopened successfully, reconciled all published row counts, and was checksum-verified. Full Python CI is green on 3.11 and 3.12, and the dashboard typecheck, coverage, Storybook build, and serial Chromium suite are green.
